newsitem.title: UK: Brazil, Europe feature in sugar freight orders.
newsitem.headline: Brazil, Europe feature in sugar freight orders.

text.p: The sugar freight market saw renewed demand for Brazilian and European ports on Monday in a continuation of the trend seen last week, shipbrokers said.

Brazilian inquiry remained centred on shipments out of the northern cane growing region although southern ports such as Paranagua still featured in freight orders towards the latter end of their sugar export cycle.
Czarnikow Rionda quoted for 18,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Paranagua to east coast Mexico for November 1/7 and repeated its earlier Rosario/U.S. Gulf and Buenaventura/Sri Lanka inquiries.
Shipbrokers said E D & F Man was still in the market for 24/25,000 tonnes from Paranagua to Morocco with Egypt/Baltic options for the end of October.
Man was also reported to have fixed a prompt 14,300-tonne cargo from the same port to Black Sea/Baltic but details of the rate achieved have yet to emerge.
North Brazilian demand was evident from major shippers Tate & Lyle and Cargill.
Tate & Lyle was in the market for 13,000 tonnes min/max bulk sugar from Recife to U.S. NH for October 20/26.
Cargill was open for 14,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Maceio or Recife to Morocco, Egypt, Mediterranean or Black Sea options for prompt shipment dates.
Elsewhere, Secretan was open with three small bagged orders from Antwerp as Europe gears up to ship sugar from its 1996/97 beet crop.
Secretan quoted for 1,500 tonnes to Riga/Tallinn for October 17/22, 3,000 tonnes with Calais option to Algiers for 10 days notice and 3,200 tonnes to Durres for October 22/27.
Secretan also quoted for 4/6,000 tonnes from Continent to Algiers for 10 days notice and 1,000 tonnes from Calais to Poti for prompt shipment.

Jean Lion was open for 14/14,300 tonnes of bagged sugar from Continent to Jeddah with Karachi option for prompt dates and was said to have fixed 13/14,300 tonnes from Continent to Damman with Jeddah/Dubai options, again for prompt dates.
Iranian shippers IRISL quoted for 14,000 tonnes of preslung bagged sugar from the European Union excluding the UK to Iran for prompt/October 31 dates.
Shyvers Savoy quoted an account order for 12,000 min/max bulk sugar from Pointe des Gallets to Marseilles for November 1/5.
CSR quoted for 20,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Queensland to Japan for November 5/15. Shipbrokers said the rate achieved on CSR's last similar order was close to $16.50.

Syria has issued an international tender to buy 13,000 tonnes of white sugar and 13,000 tonnes of raws for shipment between November 25 and December 25, with November 5 set as the final date for bids to be received.
